summary:
Our project is an entertaining and educational app designed for adolescents and teenagers, bringing the stories of abandoned space equipment to life. Since the 1960s, NASA and other space agencies have sent incredible machines to explore the Moon, Mars and beyond. But what happens to these machines when their missions end? Our app imagines what these forgotten explorers might be thinking and feeling, using humour, sarcasm and relatable personalities to tell their stories.

Through funny conversations, witty comments and interesting facts, users can discover the purpose of different space machines, their missions and the scientific discoveries they helped make. By combining education with creativity and humour, our project makes space exploration more engaging and accessible to younger audiences. It also encourages users to appreciate the technology and achievements behind space exploration, while reminding them that even machines have stories worth telling.
details:
Our project is an educational and entertaining app designed for adolescents and teenagers. It introduces users to space equipment that has been left behind after completing missions to the Moon, Mars and beyond. The app shares information about these machines, their original purposes and the discoveries they helped make. What makes it different is that we give the equipment imaginary personalities, thoughts and feelings, using humour, sarcasm and funny comments to make learning more enjoyable.

We wanted to create something that is easy to navigate, simple to understand and useful as a source of information. Our aim is to encourage young people to become more interested in space exploration without making learning feel like a classroom lesson. We hope users will walk away having learned something new while also having a laugh.

Creativity was an important part of our project. Instead of presenting facts in a traditional way, we imagined what abandoned space equipment might say if it could talk. For example, a forgotten Mars rover might complain about being left alone or sarcastically question why nobody has come to collect it!

Our team consisted of three members doing most of the development work, with one supervisor guiding and supporting us along the way. We may not have been the quickest thinkers or the most technically experienced team, but we were determined to give the project our best effort and learn as we went.

The tools we used included C# (Visual Studio) for programming and Clip Studio for creative artwork and visual elements. Throughout development, we considered ease of navigation, clear information, age-appropriate humour, creativity and making the app enjoyable for our intended audience.

Ultimately, we wanted to prove that learning about science and space does not have to be complicated or boring. Sometimes, a little humour and imagination can make even an abandoned piece of space equipment interesting!
